summary: Feed s154_double to IDS is degraded: 50% of traffic missing required VLAN 20 tags and traffic bursts to 1.66 Gbps exceed the 1 Gbps IDS port (166% capacity). IDS has blind spot on VLAN 20 and will drop packets during bursts.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN/TAP trunk is stripping 802.1Q tags or not forwarding VLAN 20. 50% of packets are untagged and VLAN 20 is completely absent despite IDS requiring VLANs 10 and 20, indicating a broker VLAN filter / trunk pruning or SPAN that removes tags.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to all traffic on VLAN 20 (50% of expected coverage). VLAN-aware signatures, segmentation policies and lateral-movement detection for VLAN 20 will not fire.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 through the packet broker to the IDS so VLAN-based detection and required coverage is restored.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate traffic bursts exceed single tool port capacity. Peak 1.66 Gbps in 1ms bursts vs 1 Gbps IDS port (166% load, 10 overloaded intervals) with no load balancing or rate control on the packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS will drop packets during bursts due to port oversubscription. With needs_full_payload=true and needs_both_directions=true, drops break TCP reassembly and flow reconstruction, causing missed exploits and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across 2+ IDS ports or upgrade to higher-speed port to keep peak below 80% utilization and prevent packet drops while preserving full payload for IDS analysis.
